entries.title: Proverbs 13:2
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Shall eat - Shall receive comfort, and benefit by his wise and profitable discourses.

entries.title: Proverbs 13:6
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Keepeth him - From that over - throw which befal sinners.

entries.title: Proverbs 13:7
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Maketh rich - Some men who have little or nothing, pretend to have great riches. Maketh rich - Some rich men profess to be poor.

entries.title: Proverbs 13:8
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Riches - Riches enable a man to redeem his life when it is in greatest danger, and poverty preserves a man from many injuries. Because they are cautious, that they may not provoke others; and because they are esteemed objects of pity.

entries.title: Proverbs 13:9
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: The light - The prosperity. Rejoiceth - Shines with a pleasant and constant brightness. Rejoicing is here ascribed to the light, as it is to the sun, Psal 19:5, metaphorically. Put out - Their felicity shall have a hidden end.

entries.title: Proverbs 13:10
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Pride - It is chiefly, pride which blows up the coals of contention. Well - advised - Who are not governed by their passions, but by prudent considerations. Wisdom - Which teaches them to avoid contention.

entries.title: Proverbs 13:12
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Hope deferred - Delays in obtaining what a man passionately desires. The desire - The good desired. A tree of life - It is satisfactory, and reviving.

entries.title: Proverbs 13:14
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: The law - The instruction, or counsel; as the word law, is frequently understood in scripture.

entries.title: Proverbs 13:15
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Giveth - Makes a man acceptable to God. Rough - Offensive and hateful to God and men, as rough ways are to a traveller.

entries.title: Proverbs 13:16
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Knowledge - Considerately and discreetly. Layeth open - By his foolish actions.

entries.title: Proverbs 13:17
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: A messenger - Who is unfaithful in the execution of that which is committed to his charge. Is health - Procures benefit, as to his master, so to himself.

entries.title: Proverbs 13:19
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Sweet - Whatsoever men earnestly desire, the enjoyment of it is sweet to them; therefore sinners rejoice in the satisfaction of their sinful lusts, and abhor all restraint of them.

entries.title: Proverbs 13:23
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: The poor - Poor persons by their diligent labours, and God's blessing often grow rich. Destroyed - Or, consumed, brought to poverty, for want of discretion.

entries.title: Proverbs 13:24
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Hateth his son - His fond affection, is as pernicious to him as hatred.
